current_activity: Charnwood: clears the Lebisey area and, with the 33rd Armoured Brigade, takes the high ground round Point 64 above Caen
notes: Event date: 8 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 313, 315). Event definition: On the first day of the attack on Caen the division completely clears the Lebisey area and, supported in the early evening by the 33rd Armoured Brigade, captures the high ground round Point 64, from which it overlooks Caen; patrols reach the outskirts but debris stops them (p. 315); on 9 July it moves into Caen (p. 316). current_activity: Holds the Maas front between Venlo and Boxmeer, attached to II Canadian Corps since 29 December; attachment ends
notes: Event date: 19 January 1945, the last day under II Canadian Corps (Stacey, p. 443; Ellis, vol. II, p. 238, says only "the middle of January"). Event definition: While the Ardennes battle is fought the division, of VIII Corps, and its front along the Maas between Venlo and Boxmeer are put under II Canadian Corps (First Canadian Army) from Second Army on 29 December 1944, so that Second Army can give its whole attention to the Ardennes; the arrangement lasts until 19 January 1945, when the division passes back to Second Army (Stacey, p. 443); Ellis calls it the 3rd Division of VIII Corps and lists it in that corps on 3 September and 14 November 1944 (notes on pp. 4 and 159), and puts the Canadian front on the Maas towards Venlo in contact with the left of VIII Corps (pp. 238, 240). Event support: two source families (Ellis, the British official history, and Stacey, the Canadian official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 4: "VIII Corps—3rd"; pp. 159-160: "VIII Corps—11th Armoured Division, 3rd and 15th Divisions"; p. 238: "the British 3rd Division of VIII Corps, and its front along the Maas as far south as Venlo, was put under II Canadian Corps"; "This arrangement lasted till the middle of January"; pp. 240-241: "where they linked with the left of VIII Corps"; Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 443: "The 3rd British Infantry Division and its front along the Maas between Venlo and Boxmeer came under the 2nd Canadian Corps from Second Army on 29 December"; p. 443: "Simonds until 19 January". Location: Well, Bergen, Limburg (new place), a village on the Maas near the middle of the front between Venlo and Boxmeer with a precision of 25 km. Location support: Stacey gives the front as along the Maas between Venlo and Boxmeer and Ellis as along the Maas as far south as Venlo (pp. 443; 238). Commander: Maj.-Gen. L. G. Whistler, commanding the 3rd Division to 21 January 1945 and again from 25 February 1945, with Maj.-Gen. A. Galloway in between (Ellis, vol. II, p. 374). current_activity: Veritable: relieves the 15th Division in XXX Corps west of Weeze; directed on Kervenheim and Winnekendonk

current_activity: Bremen: from 20 April closes in round the city with three other divisions of XXX Corps; patches of stiff opposition
notes: Event date: 20 April 1945 (the day from which the divisions closed in) (Ellis, vol. II, p. 316). Event definition: From 20 April the four infantry divisions of XXX Corps (the 3rd, 43rd, 51st and 52nd) close in round the city of Bremen, finding patches of stiff opposition, especially on the high ground in the north, where 83 Group of the Royal Air Force helps to loosen some of the enemy positions; the fighting continues through the next five days, and on the 25th, after heavy and medium bomber attacks, the city itself is assaulted with the support of two heavy and four medium regiments of artillery (p. 316); the page does not say which part of the ring the division held. Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 316: "From the 2oth of April the four infantry divisions of XXX Corps (grd, 43rd, 51st and 52nd) closed in round the city of Bremen"; "find- ing patches of stiff opposition, especially on high ground in the north". Location: Bremen (existing place PL0625), the city the four divisions closed in on with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is the city of Bremen, which the four divisions encircled; the page gives no sector for the division and its headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Bremen as the city the four divisions closed in round (p. 316).
